notes:
Summary: Enterprise messaging provider evaluating Redwood Dedicated for latency-sensitive customer conversations and live voice assistants. Primary ask: guaranteed throughput during business hours and predictable p95 latency for chat completions. Team is conservative on on-prem/VPC controls and wants clear SLA language around latency and failover.

From discovery call (02/18):
- Customer profile: multi-tenant messaging platform, 30M monthly active users, peak concurrent chat QPS spikes during campaign windows.
- Workload mix: 70% short chat completions (~40-120 tokens), 20% streaming voice->text->LLM interactions (longer tokens), 10% embeddings for semantic routing.
- Baseline traffic sample (requested): average steady QPS ~120 across US regions, 5-minute peak bursts to ~920 QPS during promotions. Typical prompt token length per completion: 80 tokens; streaming flows average 600 tokens per session.
- Target latency SLOs: p95 <= 120ms for non-streaming chat steps, end-to-end streaming latency < 500ms visible tokens. Business requirement: deterministic latency for paid tiers.
- Cost sensitivity: medium; willing to commit to reserved capacity if unit cost predictable and autoscale burst allowed.

Technical notes / initial ops thinking:
- Candidate model mix: mix of 13B Q4/8 quantized for high-throughput short chats, with fallback to 70B-quantized for long-form summarization; also local on-prem smaller LLMs for PII-sensitive flows.
- Performance knobs discussed: KV cache for multi-turn sessions, prefix caching for templated responses, dynamic batching windows (10-30ms target) to balance p95 and throughput.
- Expected tokens/sec demand estimate (rough): steady-state tokens/sec ~9,600 t/s (120 QPS * 80 tokens), burst tokens/sec ~73,600 t/s (920 QPS * 80 tokens) ignoring streaming sessions. Streaming adds variable load; recommend sample-based simulation.
- SLA negotiation points: uptime 99.9% (enterprise), latency credit formula for missed p95 targets, explicit fallback policy (route to hosted model variant or degraded throughput), maintenance blackout windows and advance notice.

Workshop plan (2-hr):
1) Pre-work: client to upload 30 days of anonymized traces + representative prompts and percent streaming flag.
2) Walkthrough of production traffic shape, identify steady vs burst windows and percent long-tail tokens.
3) Run capacity model: baseline QPS, tokens/sec, per-GPU token/sec profile for suggested model quantizations.
4) Output: recommended reserved GPU count, burst pool sizing, suggested autoscale policy, expected p95 under modeled batching and cache assumptions, cost estimate.

Deliverables after workshop: short report (1-2 pages) with recommended reserved capacity, headroom buffer %, estimated monthly cost, tradeoffs matrix (latency vs cost), and suggested SLA language snippets.

Quotes / callouts: "We need predictable response times for our premium tier — last Black Friday spiked latency and we lost conversions." - Head of Product.

Internal AE notes: prioritize collection of real traces; emphasize Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/caching to reduce reserved GPU needs. Procurement will want explicit commit/rollback clauses in SLA.
